title: Pipeline Graph: inspect real provenance and missing artifacts
description: Read actual artifact records, distinguish missing files from missing provenance, filter the graph and copy its full Graphviz representation without rerunning analysis.
objectives: Open Pipeline graph under Help and choose an existing project.
Compare recorded provenance with actual file presence and understand unrecorded dependencies.
Use Current, Stale and Missing filters without mistaking hidden nodes for absent records.
Redraw safely and copy the full graph, then use the appropriate workflow to investigate.
prerequisite: Use the real External Masks project and the completed Data Manager cleanup demonstration. This recording reads a byte-verified copy of that archived, post-cleanup snapshot at the historical project path inside an isolated namespace; original data and registry records are not rewritten. A separate real Batch Runner conversion illustrates absent provenance, not an unprocessed experiment. All 131 original project files, 26 archive files and seven conversion files remain unchanged. Three historical project records have no recorded input edges; the archive's fourth record belongs to another project path. No deletion, analysis, dedicated download, live image preview, Plot control, AI request or recovery run occurs here.

scenes.narration: Open Help, then Pipeline graph. This screen inspects recorded outputs and their dependencies; it does not execute the pipeline. We use acquired-data outputs from External Masks and the genuine Data Manager cleanup example, on private copies. Follow those lessons for producing and safely managing the data.

Browse to the converted-image folder first. Its Batch Runner conversion completed, but no artifact output was registered here, so this graph is empty. That is missing provenance, not proof that no processing happened. Declared order describes possible module dependencies; it is not a history of completed runs.

Choose the measured project's post-cleanup snapshot. Three historical records appear: a measurement database, crops and a resource log. Two paths still exist, while the cropped-image folder really was removed in the earlier private cleanup. This recording removes nothing, and the original experimental project remains intact.

Click the measurement-database box and widen the details with the divider. Read its path, role, run identifier, production time, spaCR version and settings digest. A digest is a fingerprint, not the full settings or a restore button. Current does not establish scientific validity or complete provenance.

Select the red crops box. Missing means its registered path is absent. Its recorded size still says about three point four megabytes in one hundred four files: one hundred three crop images and their format record. That is historical size, not disk usage now, and not one hundred four cells.

The resource log is a separate artifact outside the project folder. Its path still exists, but it was not moved into the archive. This graph has no recorded input edges. Nothing was derived from this means no downstream dependency was recorded here, not that the scientific outputs were independent.

Turn off Current to isolate the missing crop artifact. Current, Stale and Missing are display filters, not operations on the files. Stale is a recorded-provenance warning; this example contains no stale artifact. There are no separate module, artifact-type or workflow-branch filters in this screen.

Turn off Missing too. No boxes remain, although the banner still reports one missing artifact out of three. In this build, the empty canvas incorrectly says nothing is registered, and the previous detail can remain visible. Check the filters before interpreting either message; hidden is not deleted.

Copy Graphviz puts the full graph on the clipboard, including hidden nodes. We checked that all three actual artifact identifiers are present and no dependency arrows were invented. This is Graphviz DOT text for use elsewhere, not a saved image or an export of only the visible selection.

Restore Current, then Missing: two boxes return, then all three. Choose a box again to align its detail with the visible graph. Display filters do not repair missing files, change provenance or select a module to rerun. Investigate the actual recorded path and upstream workflow before taking action.

Redraw rereads the registry and checks the artifacts again. Our records and file bytes remain unchanged. Use Run History for saved settings and journals, or Data Manager for explicit cleanup. In Python, spacr.pipeline_graph provides build_graph and to_dot. No regeneration or scientific validation is performed by this inspection.
